guide_title: New to FPV? What you need for a build
guide_lead: A quad needs the five parts below. Pick one size and keep every part in that size: the 3-inch and the 5-inch builds use different boards, frames and motors. Each name opens that exact part. The flight controller and ESC (the stack) are paid stock; the other parts are funding targets.
guide_role_fc: The onboard computer. It keeps the quad stable and turns your stick commands into motor commands.
guide_role_esc: Takes battery power and drives the four motors. Take the same size as the flight controller.
guide_role_frame: The carbon body. Everything else bolts onto it.
guide_role_motors: One motor per arm, so a quad needs four.
guide_role_receiver: Picks up the commands from your radio and passes them to the flight controller.
guide_also_title: You will also need (not sold here)
guide_ships: Batch 1 of the flight controller and ESC is paid for and {stack_ships}.
guide_when_body: The frame, motors and receiver each have a funding target and ship about 10 weeks after it is reached. One order ships in one parcel when its last item is ready, so if you want the flight controller and ESC in October, order them on their own. Each order pays its own shipping.
guide_add_waits: The {parts} are funding targets. Add them now and the whole parcel waits for them, or order the stack now and the rest later (shipping is paid again).
guide_dji_title: Flying DJI goggles? What carries over
guide_dji_body: DJI goggles pair with a DJI O3 or O4 air unit on the quad: the air unit is the camera and video transmitter in one. Which air unit works depends on your goggle model: check DJI's compatibility list for your goggles before you buy one. The OpenFrame also takes analog, Walksnail and HDZero video systems, each with its own goggles.

The OpenRX receiver needs a radio with an ExpressLRS transmitter. Any radio with ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz built in works: look for "ELRS 2.4 GHz internal" in the radio listing. A radio with a module bay and an ExpressLRS module also works. A DJI remote controller or motion controller does not use ExpressLRS and cannot control the OpenRX.

After it arrives, three steps. 1. Plug the flight controller into your computer over USB-C and set it up in [Betaflight Configurator](https://github.com/betaflight/betaflight-configurator), which is free.

2. Check the receiver's ExpressLRS version: the receiver opens a web page over Wi-Fi that shows it, and the free [ExpressLRS Configurator](https://github.com/ExpressLRS/ExpressLRS-Configurator) updates it. The radio and the receiver must be on the same ExpressLRS major version.

3. Bind: set the same binding phrase on the radio and the receiver, or put the receiver in bind mode and press Bind on the radio. The quick-start card in the box and the [ExpressLRS binding guide](https://www.expresslrs.org/quick-start/binding/) show the steps. Questions go to [Support](/support).
help_whoop: There are no whoop-size parts. The smallest OpenDrone build is 3-inch: [see what a 3-inch build needs](/products#build-3-inch). The OpenRX Lite below is a 10.0 × 11.5 mm ExpressLRS receiver with a CRSF output and a 5 V input.
help_video_radio: We do not sell goggles, radios, cameras or video transmitters. Your goggles pair with the video system on the quad: DJI goggles with a DJI O3 or O4 air unit (which one depends on your goggle model, so check DJI's compatibility list first), analog goggles with an analog camera and transmitter. The OpenFrame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems. The OpenRX receivers need a radio with an ExpressLRS transmitter; a DJI remote controller cannot. [Which radio to get, and how binding works](/products#coming-from-dji).
help_size: OpenDrone makes 3-inch and 5-inch parts. There is no 7-inch or long-range frame: the largest build is the [5-inch build](/products#build-5-inch). The 30x30 flight controller and ESC mount on 30.5 × 30.5 mm holes, the usual stack pattern on 7-inch frames, and take up to 8S: see the [30x30 flight controller](/products/openfc-lite?Model=30%C3%9730) for its full spec table. For a longer radio link, the OpenRX Mono and Gemini add a sub-GHz band.
help_gps: OpenDrone does not sell a GPS module. See [what a build needs](/products#new-to-fpv).
picker_label: New to FPV? Pick a build:
guide_receiver_swap: Have a 900 MHz radio module? Pick the [Mono or Gemini](/products/openrx?Model=Gemini) instead.
guide_also_3inch: A radio with ExpressLRS 2.4 GHz built in: look for "ELRS 2.4 GHz internal" in the radio listing. [How the radio and receiver pair](/products#coming-from-dji).

A LiPo battery and a charger. Battery size depends on the motor: we publish the cell count and a battery size for each build together with the final motor KV. Until then, do not buy a battery for this build.

To fly through the camera: an FPV camera and video transmitter (or one digital air unit), and goggles. The frame takes analog, DJI, Walksnail and HDZero video systems. [Which goggles work with what](/products#coming-from-dji).
A soldering iron, solder and flux: a build is soldered together. [Questions about building](/support).

Setup software, both free: [Betaflight Configurator](https://github.com/betaflight/betaflight-configurator) for the flight controller and the [ExpressLRS Configurator](https://github.com/ExpressLRS/ExpressLRS-Configurator) for the receiver. [The three steps after it arrives](/products#coming-from-dji).

help_spare: Every part is sold on its own, so a crashed quad needs only the broken part: each flight controller and ESC size, each frame and single motors. Spare arms and plates: [OpenFrame spare parts](/products/openframe-spares), sold out for now. The warranty covers defects, not crash damage: see [Warranty](/warranty).
help_gift: Buying for someone else? The flight controller and ESC ship from late October 2026. The other parts ship by 11 March 2027 if their funding target is reached; if not, you choose a refund or to keep waiting. The order can go to the recipient's address. [Buying as a gift](/preorder#gift).
guide_also_note: Radio, goggles and video system usually cost more than the drone parts; many pilots already own them. Each line below links to a plain explainer.
